title: Power Pages: site analytics and server logging configuration
summary: The roadmap facts, administrative paths and configuration-upload command are supported. The page should narrow its assurance about autonomous actions, qualify the analytics dashboard and IP-storage guidance, and cite the Azure billing and access-control documentation.

claims.claim: Makers configure the planned analytics by opening the setup workspace and adding the analytics provider script.

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide analytics and server-logging policy is documented on the UI or automation surfaces as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages site analytics server logging tenant wide policy disable analytics Power Platform API administration PowerShell; Power Pages analytics tenant switch Application Insights. Opened Learn telemetry-monitoring, admin-roles, configure-site-settings and Power Platform API Websites.

claims.claim: Diagnostic Blob logging is enabled in Power Platform admin center through Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Site Actions > Enable diagnostics logs.
claims.quote: Under the Resources section, select Power Pages sites. ... Select your website. ... From the Site Actions menu, select Enable diagnostics logs.

claims.claim: A dedicated automation equivalent for enabling diagnostic Blob logging is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable diagnostic logging API Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell Blob storage; "pac power-pages" "diagnostic"; "Power Pages" "diagnostic logging" "PowerShell". Read view-portal-error-log, Power Platform API Websites operations and PAC search results.

claims.claim: The new Power Platform admin center exposes traffic analytics at Manage > Products > Power Pages > Analytics (preview).
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Manage. ... Under Products, select Power Pages and then select Analytics (preview).

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the site traffic analytics dashboard is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages traffic analytics dashboard API Power Platform API pac pages PowerShell; "Power Pages" "analytics" "API" "traffic". Read admin-center-analytics, PAC pages results and the Power Platform API Websites operations list; no dashboard equivalent appeared.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 administrators, Power Platform administrators and System administrators for their environments can access the analytics dashboard.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 administrator; Power Platform administrator; System administrator (You can only see environments for which you're a system administrator.)

claims.claim: The dashboard covers websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and site.
claims.quote: Each chart displays the DAU, WAU, and MAU for all the sites in the selected environment. ... Traffic reports are available only for public sites. Private sites aren't included in these reports.
claims.fix: Replace the dashboard clause with: 'The admin analytics dashboard covers public websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and Site ID; private sites are not included.'

claims.claim: Site settings are managed through Website > Site settings in the Power Pages Management app.
claims.quote: Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.

claims.claim: pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <model-version> uploads site configuration to the current Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Upload portal website content to the current Dataverse environment. ... path: Path where the website content is stored ... modelVersion: 1 or 2

claims.claim: The UserTrace/Debug site setting controls the diagnostic tracing described by the Power Pages DevTools documentation.
claims.quote: To enable the diagnostic setting for a public website: ... Add or update the Site Setting with the name UserTrace/Debug. ... Set the value to true.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: PAC CLI paragraph
claims.claim: Downloading, editing and uploading site settings deploys configuration rather than invoking a dedicated logging toggle.
claims.quote: once all customizations or changes are saved, you can upload the website configuration back to Microsoft Dataverse. ... adx_sitesetting

claims.claim: Application Insights masks stored IP addresses by default.
claims.quote: By default, IP addresses are temporarily collected but not stored. ... The address is then discarded, and 0.0.0.0 is written to the client_IP field.

claims.claim: Retaining IP addresses requires setting the Application Insights component's DisableIpMasking property to true.
claims.quote: To enable IP collection and storage, the DisableIpMasking property of the Application Insights component must be set to true. ... DisableIpMasking applies to classic Application Insights ingestion.
claims.fix: Narrow the second clause to: 'For classic Application Insights ingestion, retaining IP addresses requires setting DisableIpMasking to true; native OTLP ingestion does not retain the address regardless of that property.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The exact fields of the planned server and access logs are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages configure site analytics server logging Application Insights licensing tenant disable policy log fields; "Power Pages" "analytics" "server" "logs" "fields". Opened devtools-addon, view-portal-error-log and faq; these describe existing logs, not the planned log schema.

claims.claim: Azure roles control access to Application Insights resources.
claims.quote: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) provides built-in roles for monitoring ... Monitoring Reader ... Access Application Insights data.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/roles-permissions-security for the Azure role-based access claim.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Application Insights uses consumption billing based on telemetry data volume.
claims.quote: The default pricing for Log Analytics is a pay-as-you-go model that's based on ingested data volume and data retention. ... the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/cost-logs#application-insights-billing for the consumption model, Azure billing and ingestion-cost statements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific Power Pages licensing and a feature-specific charge have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages analytics Application Insights server logging licensing analytics. Opened power-pages/go-live/assign-licensing; read Power Platform licensing FAQ Power Pages excerpts and the roadmap. General site licensing is published, but no feature-specific requirement or charge appeared.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects metered Azure Application Insights ingestion.
claims.quote: the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located. For this reason, you can use all options of the Log Analytics pricing model, including commitment tiers, along with pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging storage paragraph
claims.claim: The tenant pays for the Azure Blob storage used for diagnostic logs.
claims.quote: When you create or use Blob Storage resources, you're charged for the following meters: ... Data storage | Per GB / per month ... Operations | Per transaction
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-plan-manage-costs#understand-the-full-billing-model-for-azure-blob-storage for the Blob storage charge.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging storage paragraph
claims.claim: Diagnostic logging writes website error logs to an Azure Blob storage account owned by the tenant.
claims.quote: configure your website to send all application errors to an Azure Blob storage account that you own.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging retention paragraph
claims.claim: Select retention period controls how long diagnostic error-log blobs are kept.
claims.quote: Select retention period: Duration to keep the portal error logs in blob storage. The error logs are deleted after the selected duration.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging retention paragraph
claims.claim: Select retention period is also available in Update diagnostic logging configuration.
claims.quote: From the Site Actions menu, select Update diagnostic logging configuration. ... Select retention period: Duration to keep the website error logs in blob storage.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging retention paragraph
claims.claim: The diagnostic logging retention UI currently displays only the default retention period of 30 days.
claims.quote: The UI currently displays only the default retention period of 30 days. Changes to the retention period are not reflected in the UI.

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging retention paragraph
claims.claim: The diagnostic Blob retention setting manages retained error logs rather than Application Insights ingestion.
claims.quote: Duration to keep the portal error logs in blob storage. The error logs are deleted after the selected duration.

claims.claim: The documented preparation for Power Pages activity logging does not require a site setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "Purview" "site setting" activity logs. Opened activity-logs-power-pages and read its prerequisites: licensing, permissions, environment auditing and Purview auditing; no site setting is specified.

claims.claim: Viewing Power Pages activity logs requires reviewing licensing and permissions.
claims.quote: To view Power Pages activity logs in Microsoft Purview, admins with the appropriate permissions need to: ... Review licensing and manage permissions.

claims.claim: Auditing must be turned on for the production environments to monitor.
claims.quote: Configure and turn on auditing for the Power Platform production environments you want to monitor

claims.quote: Manage auditing in Microsoft Purview and assign either the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in Microsoft Purview to you.

claims.claim: The Power Pages admin roles page lists roles by administrative task.
claims.quote: The following table lists different administrative tasks for Power Pages, and the roles required to do that task.

claims.claim: The feature has no autonomous actions and only observes and reports.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "site analytics" "server logging" autonomous actions. Read the roadmap, devtools-addon, view-portal-error-log and telemetry-monitoring. They describe telemetry and debugging, but do not state the exhaustive assurance 'None'.
claims.fix: Replace 'None. The feature observes and reports.' with 'The roadmap describes telemetry and analytics, not autonomous remediation.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks readers to review.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Choose the Azure subscription, region and retention for Application Insights'; 'Name who may view logs'; 'Audit access to the Application Insights resource.' Table: diagnostic Blob logs, traffic analytics, trace/debug logging, tenant-wide policy.
claims.fix: The checklist's Application Insights subscription, region, retention and resource-access checks have no corresponding controls-table rows. No new rows are requested by this correction.
